title: Finite two-term etale local models of the naive cotangent complex
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to Y$ a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $f$ is locally of finite presentation, meaning locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. There is a jointly surjective family of etale scheme charts $u_i:U_i\to X$ and, on each small etale site $(U_i)_{\mathrm{et}}$, a two-term complex $[\mathcal F_i^{-1}\xrightarrow{d_i}\mathcal F_i^0]$ in degrees $-1,0$ with an isomorphism
$$\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}|_{(U_i)_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq[\mathcal F_i^{-1}\xrightarrow{d_i}\mathcal F_i^0]\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_{U_i})$$
[def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Both terms are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]; $\mathcal F_i^{-1}$ is of finite type and $\mathcal F_i^0$ is of finite presentation. For a module sheaf on these sites, finite type means locally admitting an epimorphism $\mathcal O^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F$ with $n<\infty$; finite presentation means locally admitting an exact presentation $\mathcal O^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F\to0$ with $m,n<\infty$. The displayed complex has zero terms in all other degrees. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D0Z, lemma-netherlander-fp (statement); etale locally quasi-isomorphic interpreted as an isomorphism in the derived category.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to Y$ and a surjective etale scheme atlas $W\to X\times_YV$. The latter fibre product is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], which also gives its surjective etale projection to $X$. Its map to $X$ is representable surjective etale by the base-change definition in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Thus $W\to X$ is surjective etale: after testing on any scheme over $X$, it is a composite of scheme etale covers, to which [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition] applies. The chart assumption [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] says that $W\to V$ is locally of finite presentation. Choose affine opens $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i\subset W$ and $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i\subset V$ covering $W$, with $U_i\to V_i$ induced by a finitely presented ring map. Write $B_i=R_i[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_i}]/(g_1,\ldots,g_{m_i})$ as allowed by that definition. The maps $U_i\to X$ form a jointly surjective etale family; open inclusions are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], so restriction to open subschemes is an etale cover refinement, again tested on schemes and composed by the same covering lemma. In the same way each composite $V_i\subset V\to Y$ is representable etale, and $U_i\to V_i\to Y$ equals $U_i\to X\to Y$ because $W\to V$ is the second projection of $W\to X\times_YV$; so $(U_i\to V_i)\to(X\to Y)$ is a commutative square with etale vertical maps.

source.place: Tag 0D0Z, lemma-netherlander-fp, reduction to affine scheme charts.

proof.text: For each square $(U_i\to V_i)\to(X\to Y)$, both vertical arrows are etale, so [lem-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-etale-localization] identifies $\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}|_{U_i}$ with $\mathrm{NL}_{U_i/V_i}$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-etale-naive-cotangent-presentation] to $P_i=R_i[x_1,\ldots,x_{n_i}]\twoheadrightarrow B_i$ with $I_i=(g_1,\ldots,g_{m_i})$. Composing the two derived isomorphisms gives the required model with terms $(I_i/I_i^2)^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $(B_i\otimes_{P_i}\Omega_{P_i/R_i})^{\sim}_{\mathrm{et}}$. This uses an isomorphism of complexes in the derived category, not merely separate cohomology identifications.

source.place: Tags 0D0W and 0D0X; more-morphisms.tex Tags 0D0I and 0D0K, affine presentation computation.

proof.text: The classes $[g_1],\ldots,[g_{m_i}]$ generate $I_i/I_i^2$ over $B_i$: writing $h=\sum_j a_jg_j$ gives $[h]=\sum_j\bar a_j[g_j]$, independent of lifts because products of elements of $I_i$ vanish modulo $I_i^2$. For the degree-zero term use [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-polynomial-extension] with $R=A=R_i$ and $e=n_i$. Here $\Omega_{R_i/R_i}=0$, since an $R_i$-derivation of $R_i$ vanishes on every element by [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Hence $\Omega_{P_i/R_i}$ is free on the $\mathrm dx_j$, and tensoring this explicit basis gives $B_i\otimes_{P_i}\Omega_{P_i/R_i}\cong B_i^{n_i}$. This module has a finite presentation with no relations.

source.place: Tag 0D0K, lemma-netherlander-fp, final paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 00RX, lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring.

proof.text: For both modules the associated Zariski sheaves are quasi-coherent and have those modules as their global sections by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]. The affine finite-type and finite-presentation criteria [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] make the degree $-1$ sheaf of finite type and the degree-zero sheaf of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] to transfer these properties to the small etale sheaves; they are quasi-coherent by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. These are exactly the local epimorphism and finite-presentation conditions in the item. The model has zero terms outside $-1,0$ by construction. Nothing used Noetherianness or finite generation of a kernel of a map between finite modules.
